title: Switching time optimization for binary quantum optimal control
contribution: A relax-round-then-retime framework for binary quantum control: TV-penalized greedy rounding of a time-discretized relaxation, then switching-time optimization of the extracted controller sequence, with O(Δt) rounding-error bounds for α = 0 and a precomputation speed-up (read as arXiv v1).
problem_entry: Fixed time discretization in quantum control costs variables and limits control quality; binary (bang-bang, optionally SOS1) control is re-posed so that switch times become variables (pp. 2-4).
key_idea: Fix which controller runs via penalized rounding (objective-based Alg. 3 or cumulative-difference Alg. 4), merge intervals, then optimize interval lengths over a simplex with SLSQP; zero-length intervals delete switches (pp. 4-6, 12-14).
assumptions: Closed unitary dynamics, equal-step piecewise-constant relaxation, bounded objectives; rounding theory only for α = 0 and under SOS1 relaxation, cumulative SOS1 violation, or quadratic SOS1 penalty with an SOS1-feasible (P); STO solved locally (pp. 2-3, 8-10, 14).
proof_devices: Back-propagator precomputation and operation counting: O(N'T^2) to O(N'+T) exponentials (Props. 1-2, pp. 7-8)
Taylor expansion of the per-step propagator with singular-value lemmas to bound O(dt^2) terms (Lemmas 1-4, Thm. 1, pp. 8-9, 32-36)
Contradiction via convex-combination weighting by continuous controls to show a controller with nonpositive first-order change exists (pp. 33-38)
Quadratic-penalty contradiction forcing the L1 SOS1 violation to vanish as T grows (Cor. 1, pp. 10-11)
Lifting N non-SOS1 controllers to 2^N SOS1 subset-controllers with identical dynamics (Cor. 2, pp. 11-12)
Eigendecomposition of each Hermitian controller once for cheap propagators in STO (p. 15)
experiments: 12 instances (energy 2/4/6 qubits, CNOT, NOT, UCCSD circuit compilation H2/LiH/BeH2) vs the coauthors' own TR+MT+ALB method; penalties tuned per instance on the comparison set; objective, TV-norm, CPU per phase; up to 16.3x acceleration; coarse grids match post-STO objective; TV-norm losses only in appendix Table 9; code on GitHub (pp. 15-27, 41).
positioning: Extends the authors' own Fei et al. [18]; credits Logsdon-Biegler for simultaneous time-point optimization and Sager et al. for sum-up rounding; critiques time-discretized GRAPE/RL approaches for cost and limited quality (pp. 3-4, 12).
writing: First/Second/Third contribution paragraph, theorems in text with proofs in appendix, strong 'significantly outperforms' in the conclusion next to a hedge that both rounding methods should be tried (pp. 4, 9, 21-22, 27).
limits_future: Depends on penalty tuning; CPU grows exponentially in qubits; future: time evolution on quantum hardware and robust control under noise (pp. 22, 27).

method_links.note: Quantum pulses re-cast as binary mixed-integer optimal control with SOS1 and TV switching penalty; sum-up rounding carried in from MIOC.
Self-built baseline (own [18]) but penalties tuned per instance on the comparison set; TV-norm losses only in appendix; 'significantly outperforms' in conclusion.
The fixed time-grid formulation is blamed for cost and quality loss and replaced by a switching-time formulation before changing the algorithm.

Precompute back propagators and eigendecompositions so each candidate evaluation is one product (pp. 7-8, 15).

title: Augmentation algorithms for total variation-regularized integer programs
contribution: Characterizes the Graver basis of TV-like integer programs on graphs as connected induced subgraphs, re-derives Kolmogorov-Shioura's exact augmentation, and gives a randomized-simplex Graver-sampling heuristic for the budget-constrained case that beats CPLEX on large image instances (read as arXiv v2).
problem_entry: Budget-constrained integer programs with separable convex terms and a TV-like regularizer on a graph are little studied and NP-hard in general; the trust-region subproblem of the Leyffer-Manns SLIP method is a case (pp. 2-5).
key_idea: Edges of the TU polytope are Graver multiples, so a primal simplex on the LP form of the augmentation subproblems is a Graver augmentation; randomize degenerate choices and budget-aware pricing to sample improving feasible moves, alternate up/down, polish to 2-optimality (pp. 9-10, 13-19).
assumptions: Univariate convex F, G, H on {0..Q}^V; with the budget the Graver basis no longer certifies optimality (heuristic); path-existence result needs a start minimizing each H_v; complementarity of split variables follows from convexity of G (pp. 2, 13-14).
proof_devices: Max-level-set connected-component lemma for conformal minimality (Lemma 2, Thm. 1, p. 9; Lemma 7, Thm. 8, pp. 11-12)
Total unimodularity implies polytope edges are Graver multiples (Remark 2, Cor. 6, pp. 8, 10)
Conformal decomposition ordered monotone in J plus convexity of H around its minimizer for a feasible improving path (Prop. 10, pp. 14-15)
Counting argument: basic solutions as rooted spanning forests (Prop. 11, pp. 15-16)
Generalized penalty approximation bound by noting the original proof uses no specific function form (Prop. 12, pp. 19-20)
Local optimality comparison: Graver-optimal implies 1-optimal, not 2-optimal (Prop. 9, p. 14)
experiments: 288 image-reconstruction instances (6 images, N in {32,64,96}, binding budgets) and public Manns-Severitt TR subproblems; 6 configurations (3 starts x p in {0,1}) with best of up to 100 trials vs CPLEX default 600 s; best-count, MIP gap vs CPLEX lower bound before/after polish, time; CPLEX wins at N=32, 20 TR instances time out without improvement; phase transition in p (pp. 21-27).
positioning: Recovers Kolmogorov-Shioura via Graver bases; places itself among Graver methods for N-fold and two-stage stochastic IPs; generalizes Manns-Severitt; admits min-cut is faster than its LP form and the connected-subgraph restriction weakens the iteration bound (pp. 3, 7, 10, 13, 19-20).
writing: Section-by-section contribution outline, explicit hedges ('we hope', 'we do not have any proof'); naming slip between smallest and largest coefficient and an alpha mismatch between appendix text and figure caption (pp. 5-6, 14, 18, 22, 25, 32-33).
limits_future: No pivot bound, no approximation guarantee, arbitrary up/down alternation, open choice of p; future: matching via alternating walks, multiple separable constraints, embedding in a trust-region method for nonlinear F (pp. 18, 27-28).

method_links.note: Own randomized primal simplex instead of a faster min-cut black box, so simplex edges are reinterpreted as Graver moves and pivots can be rejected or biased by budget use.
Calibrated claim 'competitive with and often outperforms'; losses reported in text (CPLEX best at N=32; 20 timeouts). Baseline is CPLEX at default settings, not self-built.
Reuses a public instance repository from Manns-Severitt, but own image instances and code only available on request.
The carried-in toolkit is integer algebra (Graver bases, TU) rather than the NLP/filter base; Leyffer's SLIP line supplies the problem.

title: A mixed-integer PDE-constrained optimization formulation for constructing electromagnetic cloaks with multiple materials
contribution: Extends the authors' MIPDECO cloaking model to several materials with SOS1 and a mass constraint, solved by a reduced-space relaxation, a single-MILP feasibility-pump-style rounding, a discrete steepest-descent trust-region method with MILP subproblems, and mesh sequencing.
problem_entry: Generalizes the group's own single-material Helmholtz cloak MIPDECO along two named axes, multiple materials and an upper bound on mass (p. 3).
key_idea: Relax in reduced space, project the relaxed permittivity onto the discrete materials by one l1 MILP with mass and SOS1, improve with a trust-region method whose subproblem is a linear MILP in the binaries, and warm-start finer control meshes from coarse integer solutions (pp. 10-12, 18).
assumptions: 2D Helmholtz with Robin boundary, box cloak on a control mesh, SOS1 per cell, mass as inequality; unique state for bounded nontrivial permittivity with k0 away from eigenfrequencies; nonconvex bilinear term, no valid outer approximation or lower bound (pp. 4-7, 11).
proof_devices: No theorems; formal-Lagrangian adjoint derivation of the reduced gradient (pp. 7-8)
Gradient with p materials per cell needs only N integrals scaled by q_i (p. 9)
Trust-region ratio test with doubling on boundary hit and floor-halving on rejection (Alg. 1, p. 12)
experiments: One geometry, k0 = 6*pi, 2 and 4 materials, control meshes 20x20/40x40/80x80 on a 128x128 FEM mesh; FEniCS, SciPy trust-constr, CPLEX 12.8; objectives and mass per stage, CPU split by component; relaxation up to 1,729,093 s; mesh sequencing better, lighter, cheaper; only internal comparisons; code not public (pp. 13-23).
positioning: Extends Haslinger's topology-optimization formulation and the authors' own MIPDECO; borrows from the feasibility pump literature; no critique of other methods (pp. 2-3, 11).
writing: Two-extension contribution statement; modelling choices justified in place; overstated conclusion that cost does not depend on the number of materials and 'optimal cloak' wording despite local results; same prior work cited as [9] and [15] (pp. 3, 6, 8, 11, 16, 22).
limits_future: Nonconvexity and no bounds, relaxation cost explodes with mesh size, mass constraint hardens the TR subproblem; future: a cost constraint (pp. 7, 14-17, 22).

method_links.note: Feasibility pump, MILP-subproblem trust region and SOS1 carried into MIPDECO; carried-in PDE uniqueness assumption checked by choosing k0 away from eigenfrequencies.
l1 rather than l2 so the rounding is an MILP; mass as inequality; reduced space because states are unique.
No external baseline, only own variants; conclusion overstates cost independence from the number of materials against Tables 2 and 4.
Code and instances not released to the public; reproduction relies on the paper's description.

transferable: Round a PDE-constrained relaxation by one l1 projection MILP onto the discrete material set with all non-PDE constraints (p. 11).
Discrete steepest-descent trust region with linear model, l1 radius and side constraints in an MILP subproblem (p. 12).
Mesh sequencing for integer controls: one relaxation on the coarsest control mesh, warm-start finer meshes from the coarse integer solution (p. 18).
